info.name: Stripe API POC 20250820
info.description:
This Postman collection demonstrates:
1. Stripe Checkout flows (Normal, Pre-Authorization, Subscription).
2. Stripe Elements (CPM) single-payment POC using Stripe Payment Intents + Plaid Transfer UI. The merchant-facing Omni Collect endpoint is intentionally not invented; the collection contains the underlying Stripe/Plaid APIs that Omni Collect will wrap.
3. Common endpoints / refund flows.

item.name: 2. Stripe Elements (CPM)
item.description:
Single-payment POC for Stripe Payment Element + Stripe Custom Payment Method (CPM) + Plaid Transfer UI.

Important frontend/API chain:
1) Run 2.1.1 to create the Stripe PaymentIntent. The response test stores `elements_cpm_payment_intent_id` and `elements_cpm_client_secret`.
2) Frontend (not Postman) uses that client secret to render Stripe Payment Element and configures `stripe_cpm_id` in Stripe.js `customPaymentMethods`.
3) If the customer selects the CPM option, the frontend branches away from Stripe payment confirmation and the backend runs 2.1.2.
4) 2.1.2 returns `transfer_intent.id`, saved as `plaid_transfer_intent_id`.
5) 2.1.3 passes that ID to Plaid `/link/token/create` and stores the returned `link_token`.
6) Frontend (not Postman) initializes Plaid Link / Transfer UI using `plaid_link_token`.
7) After Plaid Link onSuccess, run 2.1.4 with the original transfer intent ID. When successful, it returns `transfer_id`, saved as `plaid_transfer_id`.
8) Use 2.1.5 and 2.1.6 to inspect the actual ACH transfer and its lifecycle events.

The merchant-facing Omni Collect endpoint is intentionally NOT modelled here because no Omni endpoint definition has been supplied. These requests represent the underlying Stripe and Plaid APIs that Omni Collect will wrap.

item.name: 2.1 - Single Payment
item.description: POC scope: one-time payment only. Stripe renders the unified Payment Element; the custom ACH option is processed outside Stripe through Plaid Transfer UI.

exec: console.log("[Elements CPM] Payment Intent ID:", jsonData.id);

request.description: Creates the PaymentIntent used by Stripe Payment Element. The CPM ID is NOT sent in this API request; `stripe_cpm_id` is used later by Stripe.js in the frontend `customPaymentMethods` configuration. The test script stores the PaymentIntent ID and client_secret.

Plaid Transfer UI flow. Creates a one-time ACH PAYMENT transfer intent. For a net-new customer flow, no Plaid account_id is supplied yet; the customer selects/connects the bank account later in Plaid Transfer UI. The returned `transfer_intent.id` is saved as `plaid_transfer_intent_id` and is the required chain value for 2.1.3.

Creates the Plaid Link token for Transfer UI. CHAIN: `plaid_transfer_intent_id` from 2.1.2 is passed as `transfer.intent_id`. The returned `link_token` is saved as `plaid_link_token` and is then used by the frontend Plaid Link SDK to open Transfer UI. If a non-default Link customization is used, add `link_customization_name` later after that Dashboard configuration is known.

Run after the customer finishes Plaid Transfer UI. CHAIN: uses the original `plaid_transfer_intent_id` from 2.1.2. If the transfer intent status is SUCCEEDED, Plaid returns `transfer_id`; the test script saves it as `plaid_transfer_id` for the next requests.
Retrieves the actual Plaid Transfer created by Transfer UI. CHAIN: uses `plaid_transfer_id` returned by 2.1.4. Use this to inspect the current ACH transfer state.

exec: console.log("[Plaid] Latest Transfer Event ID:", maxEventId);

request.description: Synchronizes Plaid Transfer lifecycle events after the stored event ID. Use the returned events to identify status changes for `plaid_transfer_id`. The test script advances `plaid_transfer_event_after_id` to the latest event returned.
